mainEntity.name: How long does whiplash take to heal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild cases often improve within a few weeks of consistent care; more significant injuries can take a few months. We reassess regularly and adjust your plan as you progress.

A whiplash grade — based on the Quebec Task Force classification, the standard grading framework — describes severity, from neck symptoms without physical signs to fracture or dislocation. A qualified clinician should assess the injury rather than relying on symptoms alone.

mainEntity.name: Can whiplash cause headaches weeks later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — cervicogenic headaches that trace back to the neck are one of the most common delayed whiplash symptoms, sometimes showing up well after the initial stiffness eases.

Yes — it's common to feel fine at the scene and then develop neck stiffness, headaches, or reduced range of motion in the hours or days that follow. Feeling okay immediately after a collision doesn't rule out whiplash; an evaluation can document any delayed-onset symptoms.

mainEntity.name: How does PIP coverage work for my visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Florida PIP generally requires initial services and care within 14 days of a motor vehicle accident. Benefit limits and payment depend on your eligibility, policy, medical necessity, and claim details.
